overview.title: AI CODE BGM STUDIO in short

blocks.html:
AI CODE BGM STUDIO takes the sound you describe in words and has Gemini build it as Web Audio API code. It runs inside Google’s Gemini Canvas, so there is nothing to install and no API key to supply.

You can play the result on the spot and take it away either as MP3 / WAV or as the code that plays the sound. That makes it a quick way to rough out background music and sound effects for SlideCast Studio.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Worth saying up front
blocks.text: Generation is a lottery. The same prompt will not give you the same quality every time, and this is not an app that produces a finished, professional track in one shot. It works best as a way to get a usable draft quickly.

blocks.html: The app itself is covered in the official manual, and the product is introduced on What is SlideCast Studio?. This page is about the other side of it — preparing the audio you drop in.

blocks.title: 🇯🇵 The app’s interface is in Japanese
blocks.text: AI CODE BGM STUDIO ships with a Japanese UI, so the screenshots on this page are Japanese. Each field is spelled out in English below, and the theme box accepts English text.

sections.title: What the app does
sections.intro: Describe what you want, press generate, and the track plays right there.

blocks.html:
While putting a video or an app together, you keep running into “a bit of background music would help here”, “I need a short sound effect”, or “let me at least get the mood right first”. Sitting down to actually compose something is a heavy way to answer that. This app is the light way.

Prompts can be as plain as these:

items: A field theme for an RPG set in a forest at night
Bright, poppy background music for a home screen
A short sound effect for a system notification

items.title: Written prompt in
items.text: Theme, purpose and mood are all you need. Every detailed setting can be left on “auto”.

items.title: Code, not a file
items.text: What comes back is the code that plays the sound, rather than a finished audio file.

items.title: Nudge it afterwards
items.text: Ask for “a little more mysterious” and it edits the current result rather than starting over.

items.title: Fill in from a reference
items.text: Feed it text, an image, a PDF or a URL and it fills in genre and mood for you.

sections.title: What you can specify
sections.intro: A one-line idea is enough, and so is a fully specified brief.

blocks.caption: 種類 = type, テーマ・コンセプト = theme and concept, 生成パターン数 = how many variations to generate

items.label: Length
items.value: In seconds (60 seconds or less recommended for BGM)

items.label: Genre
items.value: Game BGM, cinematic, ambient, 8-bit chiptune, EDM / trance, lo-fi hip hop, system sound effects, and more

items.label: Instruments
items.value: Piano, synth pad, strings, drums, bells and others (multiple selection)

items.label: Also
items.value: A free-text notes field, plus auto-fill from reference material or a URL

blocks.html:
Anything you are unsure about can be left on おまかせ (auto). Writing only the theme, listening to what comes back, and adding settings afterwards is often the faster route.

Open 「資料・URLから詳細を自動設定」(fill in details from a reference or URL) and hand it text, an image or a PDF, and it fills in the genre and mood fields for you. References are abstracted rather than copied, which suits the case where you want a similar atmosphere without reproducing the source.

blocks.title: 🎲 Start with three patterns
blocks.text: Setting the pattern count to 3 gives you three different takes on the same brief at once. It finds a keeper faster than regenerating one track at a time.

sections.title: Getting the audio and the code out
sections.intro: Anything you like can be saved as sound, as code, or both.

blocks.caption: The right-hand end of the playback bar saves either the audio file or the generated code

items: Save the audio as MP3 or WAV
Download the generated code as a .js file
Download every pattern at once when you generated several
Load a downloaded file back in to preview it
Paste code in and apply it to play it straight away
Up to 20 items of history — undo and redo as far back as you need

blocks.html: Keeping the code alongside the audio is the point of the app. It makes the small later edits easy — nudging the volume or the length, or rebuilding the same piece at a different duration. Loop playback and volume are in the app too, so the “does this work?” check happens before anything reaches your video.

sections.title: Nudging the result into shape
sections.intro: The app is built for roughing something out and then closing in on it.

blocks.alt: The follow-up instruction box with an apply button, and undo and redo buttons underneath
blocks.caption: 追加演出指示 = follow-up instructions; the note above the box promises the smallest change that satisfies them

blocks.html: A follow-up instruction is a diff against the current result, not a fresh start, so the parts you already like survive while the direction shifts.

items: Make it a little more mysterious
Open quietly for the first two seconds
End on a sense of achievement

blocks.title: ↩️ Nothing is one-way
blocks.text: Undo and redo walk back through the last 20 results, so you can afford to ask for something drastic and simply step back if it overshoots.

sections.title: Using it with SlideCast Studio
sections.intro: Trade the time you spend hunting for a track for the time it takes to make one.

blocks.html: SlideCast Studio lets you set background music and sound effects, but there is a common case where you have no strong preference and simply do not want to go looking for a track. That is the gap this app fills.

items.title: Put the mood of the video into words
items.text: Something like “quiet ambient bed for a calm explainer video” — purpose plus atmosphere.

items.title: Set a length and generate
items.text: 60 seconds or less is recommended for BGM. For a long video, a shorter loopable piece repeated in SlideCast Studio is easier to work with.

items.title: Export as MP3
items.text: Use the ↓ MP3 button on the playback bar.

items.title: Load it into SlideCast Studio
items.text: Add it to a BGM track. Short pieces generated as sound effects also work as text-advance or slide-transition sounds.

blocks.title: 🎵 Up to 10 BGM tracks
blocks.text: SlideCast Studio can layer several BGM tracks: one bed across the whole video, plus a second that only lifts the moment you want to emphasise. The official manual has the details.

sections.title: Setting expectations honestly
sections.intro: What it is good at, and what it is not.

blocks.html:
To be straight about it: the app is not a magic box. Generation is a lottery, and much the same brief will give you “that one is great” one moment and “not quite” the next. That comes from Gemini generating code, and from the limits of making sound in a browser at all.

And frankly, asking any AI service “write me background music as code only, and let me download it as MP3” gets you something similar. The idea is not exotic.

What is tedious in practice is rebuilding the prompt every time, pasting the returned code somewhere, and rigging up a way to hear it. This app is that loop, packaged so you do not repeat it.
